name: e2e
description: Next generation e2e testing framework for web and mobile apps.
one_liner: A testing tool where you describe a user goal in plain English (like 'upgrade to Pro') and a robot clicks through your website or app to check it actually works, then remembers the steps so it's fast and cheap to re-check later.
buyer: A QA lead or engineering manager at a 10-50 person software company who is tired of brittle click-recorder tests breaking every release.
business_use_cases: A SaaS company wires it into every pull request so a broken checkout flow is caught before it ships, not after a customer complains.
A QA agency offers 'AI-written regression suites' as a service to clients who have no in-house test coverage.
An e-commerce team runs it nightly against staging to catch a broken 'add to cart' button across ten device sizes.

money_ideas.idea: Run a boutique QA-as-a-service shop: write and maintain e2e test suites for small SaaS teams who can't afford a QA hire.
Build and sell a hosted dashboard that aggregates test runs, flaky-test detection, and PR comments for teams self-hosting the open-source core.

steal_this: This weekend, package a 'free broken-checkout audit': point the tool at five local e-commerce sites, screenshot the failures, and use that as a lead-gen offer for a paid QA retainer.
